subject.title: RFC: Readiness Conditions and Standard Hosting Profiles

question: Should OpenClaw accept the full canonical readiness-condition, plugin-provider, standard hosting-profile, configuration, and CLI contract, or initially accept only the canonical core-condition and compatibility-projection foundation?
rationale: The proposal creates durable public API and support commitments across several core surfaces, and neither current main nor repository policy determines the intended permanent scope.

options.title: Accept a staged foundation
options.body: Approve canonical core conditions and legacy compatibility projections first, then gate providers, profiles, and the CLI through follow-up review and proof.

options.title: Accept the full contract
options.body: Approve all proposed surfaces together after explicit compatibility, upgrade, and packaged-hosting proof review.

options.title: Decline core ownership
options.body: Keep advanced hosting composition outside core and close the RFC direction and its implementation candidate.

recommendation.title: Accept a staged foundation
recommendation.body: Approve canonical core conditions and legacy compatibility projections first, then gate providers, profiles, and the CLI through follow-up review and proof.

likelyOwner.reason: Repository history most directly connects this person to the RFC lifecycle and acceptance process, with Gateway owners available for technical review.
